summary: The proposal has a concrete technical topic, a relevant problem context, and a preliminary implementation direction involving Artemis and GitLab CI. However, it is not ready for submission because several required sections are missing, the objective structure and AI transparency statement are absent, the bibliography is too short, only one figure is provided, and the schedule does not follow the required agile iteration model.

findings.title: Required Sections Are Missing
findings.description: The proposal does not contain the required Introduction, Motivation, or Objective section. Section 4 instead presents system requirements and a workflow, while Section 5 presents expected findings. Add the required sections with the prescribed content and numbering.

findings.title: Objective Structure Is Missing
findings.description: The required Objective section is absent. Add a short introduction, a one-line bullet list containing 3–4 high-level objectives, and one subsection for each objective; each subsection must contain at least two paragraphs.

findings.title: AI Transparency Statement Is Missing
findings.description: No AI transparency statement is included. Add a first-person statement naming the specific AI tools used, their purposes, the sections in which they were used, and confirming that all AI-generated text was carefully checked.

findings.title: Minimum Figure Count Is Not Met
findings.description: The proposal contains only one figure, but at least two figures or diagrams are required. Add a second meaningful figure or mockup, preferably an activity, component, or class diagram if Figure 1 is not intended as a valid UML diagram.

locations.section: System Requirements and Top Level Design
locations.quote: Figure 1: Depiction of the top-level workfow of the interactions in relation to Artemis and GitLab CI

findings.title: Bibliography Contains Too Few Publications
findings.description: The bibliography contains only five entries, below the required minimum of 6–8 publications. Add at least one, preferably several, additional peer-reviewed scientific publications. Rename the References section to Bibliography if that is the required section label.

locations.quote: References

findings.title: Schedule Does Not Use Agile Iterations
findings.description: The schedule is organized as isolated weekly milestones rather than 2–4-week agile iterations. Reorganize it into iterations with measurable, end-to-end deliverables tied explicitly to the high-level objectives, rather than separating work into disconnected implementation, model, and configuration tasks.

locations.quote: April – 2nd week: Docker GitLab CI Runner confguration – 4th week: prototype implementation: Connectivity to GitLab CI
May – 3nd week: prototype implementation: Artemis API for confguration
June – 4th week: prototype implementation: Sending build results to Artemis – 4th week: Models (parallel to prototype implementation) – 4th week: Requirements (parallel to prototype implementation)

findings.title: Schedule Contains Prohibited Tasks
findings.description: The schedule includes prohibited requirements-gathering, documentation, thesis-writing, and review tasks. Replace these with development or research deliverables; requirements should be handled through the backlog within iterations rather than as a dedicated task, and thesis writing should not appear in the development schedule.

locations.quote: 4th week: Requirements (parallel to prototype implementation)
September – 2nd week: Documentation for installation and confguration of Artemis with GitLab CI
October: Writing . . .
November – 2nd week: Thesis ready for review – 3rd week: Review fnished
December – 1st week: Thesis

findings.title: Figure Reference and Caption Are Insufficient
findings.description: The figure is not explicitly referenced by figure number in the surrounding prose, and its caption is not sufficiently extensive for the caption requirement. Add an explicit reference such as “Figure 1 shows…” and expand the caption to explain the actors, systems, numbered interactions, and relevance to the proposed architecture.

findings.title: Passive Voice Obscures Actors
findings.description: The proposal uses passive or impersonal constructions extensively, which obscures the responsible actor. Rewrite sentences with explicit subjects, for example, identify who copies the repository, updates the build plans, or fetches the configuration instead of using constructions such as “is copied” and “must be updated.”

locations.quote: The student base repository **is copied** [Krusche18].
the build plans **must be updated manually** in the CI Server.
the lecture **is split up** into multiple iterations

findings.title: Forbidden Sentence Starters Occur
findings.description: Several sentences begin with forbidden starters. Rewrite these sentences so that they begin with a direct subject or an independent clause.

locations.quote: **Since** some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the efort required to maintain the servers.
**To** achieve this goal, Artemis uses a Version Control (VC) and Continuous Integration (CI) server.
**In order to** implement this idea, the lecture is split up into multiple iterations.

**Since** the benefts of using CI are quite high and nearly half of the developers who do not use CI mention a lack of familiarity as the reason for not using a CI service, it is useful to teach the concepts of CI at university [Hilton16].

findings.title: API Is Not Defined
findings.description: The abbreviation API is used without being defined at first use. Expand it as “application programming interface (API)” before using the abbreviation throughout the proposal.

locations.quote: This system supports the provision of the build plan via the Artemis **API**.
The build plan can be made available via the **API** of Artemis.
